<description>
When this feature is unavailable, `#cmakedefine` leaves its macro undefined, triggering `-Wundef`. I noticed this while building the kernel for iOs.

Use `#cmakedefine01` to always generate 0 or 1.
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-11-15] c:6897315091 comment by hebasto (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Is this concern aesthetic or technical?

However, I agree that using `#if defined(...)` poses a problem. We can't spot a typo in the macro name, for example `#if defined(HAVE_SUSTEM)`. Also see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36874.

[quoted text omitted]
In this case, it does not change behavior when `bitcoin-build-config.h` contains `#define HAVE_SYSTEM 1`. And it will trigger `-Wundef` when the macro is undefined.

The problem of detecting misused directives in the source code remains for `#cmakedefine01` as well. Perhaps this is a task for the linter.

[quoted text omitted]
The current usage is not uniform either. For example, here are the different patterns for configuration macro definitions:
1. `#define HAVE_FOO` or undefined -- is not used.
2. `#define HAVE_FOO 1` or undefined:
```console
$ git grep '#cmakedefine ' -- cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in | wc -l
18
```
3. `#define HAVE_FOO 1` or `#define HAVE_FOO 0`:
```console
$ git grep '#cmakedefine01' -- cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in | wc -l
4
```

[quoted text omitted]
This approach gives us free protection against a misspelled macro name, which will trigger the `-Wundef` compiler warning.

Here are some useful external resources:
- https://sourceware.org/glibc/wiki/Wundef
- https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/html_node/Conditional-Compilation.html
- https://libcxx.llvm.org/CodingGuidelines.html#define-configuration-macros-to-0-or-1

---

Bottom line: I agree with this PR change. I'd really like to see here a new linter check that prevents accidental misuse of `#ifdef`, `#ifndef` or `defined()` for configuration macros set via `#cmakedefine01`.
</new_statements>
